memory_lessons.applicability: The existing OpenMP result supports testing another row-level work-sharing form, but the aggregate time alone cannot identify whether region overhead or scaling caused the difference.
memory_lessons.claim: The prior OpenMP candidate was correct and measured 0.2396 s versus the correct serial baseline at 0.4575 s; no per-thread timing breakdown is present in the supplied observations.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the flattened static-row variant under the official one- and four-core settings and compare it with the collapsed-loop candidate.

proposal.hypothesis: The catalog has one distinct OpenMP candidate, valid at 0.2396 s versus the serial baseline at 0.4575 s, but the supplied aggregate times do not isolate one- versus four-thread behavior. This candidate retains the previous serial cutoff and per-timestep/persistent-region split while contrasting its collapsed 2-D row scheduling with a single flattened, static row loop. Flattening may simplify work-sharing setup, though per-row y/z index mapping may offset that; official measurements at both thread budgets are needed to assess it.

retained: Preserved the serial stencil computation, initialization, and low-work serial path.
Implemented OpenMP work sharing over one flattened y/z row iteration space with schedule(static), instead of a collapsed two-loop schedule.
Retained a parallel region per timestep for large one-thread calls and a persistent region across timesteps for larger thread budgets, with num_threads(threads).
